icons.label: Pluripotent stem
icons.description: Round embryonic stem cell with a very large central nucleus and scant teal cytoplasm.
icons.biologicalBasis: Pluripotent stem cells have a high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio, prominent nucleoli, and relatively sparse cytoplasmic specialization.

icons.label: Blood stem cell
icons.description: Round hematopoietic stem cell with a prominent nucleus, thin purple cytoplasm, and subtle membrane ruffles.
icons.biologicalBasis: Hematopoietic stem cells are non-adherent suspension cells; their compact morphology and limited cytoplasm distinguish them from mature myeloid cells.

icons.label: Lymphoid progenitor
icons.description: Small round common lymphoid progenitor with a large nucleus and light-blue cytoplasmic rim.
icons.biologicalBasis: Early lymphoid progenitors retain a high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio and lack the lineage-specific granules of mature leukocytes.

icons.label: Myeloid progenitor
icons.description: Round common myeloid progenitor with moderate nucleus and sparse azurophilic granules.
icons.biologicalBasis: Myeloid commitment is accompanied by increasing cytoplasm and the first primary granules before mature lineage-specific granulation develops.

icons.label: T-cell precursor
icons.description: Round T-cell precursor with a large nucleus, thin blue cytoplasm, and sparse immature surface receptors.
icons.biologicalBasis: T-lineage precursors are lymphoblast-like cells whose cytoplasm remains scant while receptor assembly and thymic selection proceed.

icons.label: B-cell precursor
icons.description: Round B-cell precursor with a large nucleus, thin green cytoplasm, and early B-lineage receptors.
icons.biologicalBasis: B-cell precursors are small lymphoid cells with condensed chromatin and limited cytoplasm before maturation into receptor-rich B cells.

icons.label: NK cell
icons.description: Round NK lymphocyte with an indented nucleus and a small set of dark cytotoxic granules.
icons.biologicalBasis: NK cells are large granular lymphocytes; perforin- and granzyme-containing lysosomal granules polarize toward target-cell contacts.

icons.label: T cell
icons.description: Small round T lymphocyte with a large nucleus, narrow blue cytoplasm, and distributed TCR complexes.
icons.biologicalBasis: Resting T cells are non-adherent lymphocytes with scant cytoplasm; T-cell receptors and CD3 complexes are distributed across the plasma membrane.

icons.label: B cell
icons.description: Small round B lymphocyte with a large nucleus and multiple Y-shaped membrane immunoglobulins.
icons.biologicalBasis: Mature B cells display clonally rearranged membrane immunoglobulin that captures cognate antigen and initiates receptor-mediated uptake.

icons.label: Plasma cell
icons.description: Oval plasma cell with eccentric clock-face nucleus, broad basophilic cytoplasm, rough ER, and perinuclear Golgi hof.
icons.biologicalBasis: Antibody-secreting plasma cells expand rough endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi; heterochromatin forms the characteristic cartwheel nucleus.

icons.label: Memory cell
icons.description: Compact memory lymphocyte with large nucleus, narrow deep-blue cytoplasm, and a small activation-memory marker.
icons.biologicalBasis: Quiescent memory lymphocytes resemble small resting lymphocytes but retain long-lived antigen-experienced receptor states.

icons.label: Immune cell
icons.description: Generic leukocyte with irregular lobed nucleus, cytoplasmic granules, and flexible cell membrane.
icons.biologicalBasis: Leukocytes use a deformable cortex for migration and lineage-dependent nuclear lobulation for movement through confined tissue spaces.

icons.label: Macrophage
icons.description: Large amoeboid macrophage with pseudopods, bean-shaped nucleus, phagosomes, lysosomes, and engulfed cargo.
icons.biologicalBasis: Macrophages extend actin-rich pseudopods around particles and route engulfed material through phagosomes to acidic lysosomes.

icons.label: Dendritic cell
icons.description: Irregular antigen-presenting cell with branching dendrites, central nucleus, endocytic vesicles, and MHC-bearing membrane.
icons.biologicalBasis: Conventional dendritic cells use extensive processes to sample tissue and present processed peptide on MHC to lymphocytes.

icons.label: Mast cell
icons.description: Round tissue mast cell packed with metachromatic secretory granules around a small central nucleus.
icons.biologicalBasis: Mast-cell granules store histamine, proteases, and other mediators that are rapidly released after receptor-driven activation.

icons.label: Neutrophil
icons.description: Round neutrophil with segmented 3–5-lobed nucleus and fine pale cytoplasmic granules.
icons.biologicalBasis: Mature neutrophils have a segmented nucleus for confined migration and distinct primary and secondary antimicrobial granules.

icons.label: Eosinophil
icons.description: Round eosinophil with bilobed nucleus and large red-orange specific granules.
icons.biologicalBasis: Eosinophil specific granules contain major basic protein and other effectors, producing the coarse eosinophilic appearance.

icons.label: Basophil
icons.description: Round basophil whose bilobed nucleus is partly obscured by large dark blue-purple granules.
icons.biologicalBasis: Basophil granules contain histamine and proteoglycans and often overlap the nucleus in conventional stained morphology.

icons.label: Monocyte
icons.description: Large monocyte with kidney-shaped nucleus, abundant grey-blue cytoplasm, and small vacuoles.
icons.biologicalBasis: Circulating monocytes have folded or reniform nuclei and lysosome-rich cytoplasm that supports differentiation into phagocytes.

icons.label: Erythrocyte
icons.description: Anucleate red biconcave disc with a broad rim and pale central depression.
icons.biologicalBasis: The biconcave membrane maximizes surface-area-to-volume ratio and deformability while mature mammalian erythrocytes lack nuclei and organelles.

icons.label: Megakaryocyte
icons.description: Very large marrow cell with polyploid multilobed nucleus and cytoplasmic extensions shedding platelets.
icons.biologicalBasis: Megakaryocytes form proplatelet extensions whose terminal cytoplasmic fragments enter marrow sinusoids as platelets.

icons.label: Platelets
icons.description: Cluster of small irregular anucleate platelet fragments with granules and short activation processes.
icons.biologicalBasis: Platelets are megakaryocyte-derived cytoplasmic fragments containing alpha and dense granules; activation produces filopodia.

icons.label: Enterocyte
icons.description: Tall packed absorptive enterocyte with apical brush border, terminal web, lateral junctions, elongated basal nucleus, and mitochondria.
icons.biologicalBasis: Enterocytes form a polarized columnar monolayer; dense apical microvilli increase absorptive surface while junctional complexes seal neighboring cells.

icons.label: Goblet cell
icons.description: Packed goblet cell with expanded apical mucin theca, narrow basal stalk, compressed basal nucleus, and secretion opening.
icons.biologicalBasis: Goblet cells package heavily glycosylated mucins into large apical granules that expand the cell apex and discharge into the lumen.

icons.label: Paneth cell
icons.description: Pyramidal crypt-base Paneth cell with basal nucleus, rough ER, and numerous bright apical antimicrobial granules.
icons.biologicalBasis: Paneth cells occupy the small-intestinal crypt base and secrete alpha-defensins, lysozyme, and other antimicrobials from apically concentrated dense-core granules.

icons.label: Endocrine cell
icons.description: Narrow enteroendocrine epithelial cell with apical sensing process and basal dense-core secretory granules facing a capillary.
icons.biologicalBasis: Enteroendocrine cells sense luminal cues and release peptide hormones basolaterally toward nerves and fenestrated capillaries.

icons.label: Tuft cell
icons.description: Narrow tuft cell with long stiff apical microvilli, actin rootlets, tubulovesicular network, and basal process.
icons.biologicalBasis: Tuft cells are polarized chemosensory epithelial cells defined by unusually long actin-supported microvilli and an apical tubulovesicular system.

icons.label: Transit-amplifying
icons.description: Packed crypt epithelial progenitor in mitosis with condensed chromosomes, spindle poles, and a beginning cleavage furrow.
icons.biologicalBasis: Transit-amplifying cells divide rapidly above the crypt stem-cell zone before differentiating along absorptive or secretory lineages.

icons.label: Stem cell
icons.description: Slender crypt-base columnar stem cell wedged between Paneth cells with basal nucleus and scant cytoplasm.
icons.biologicalBasis: LGR5-positive crypt-base columnar stem cells alternate with Paneth cells and continuously generate the intestinal epithelial lineages.

icons.label: M cell
icons.description: Follicle-associated epithelial M cell with flat sparse-microfold apex, captured antigen, transcytotic vesicles, and a basolateral lymphocyte pocket.
icons.biologicalBasis: M cells sample luminal particles and deliver them across the epithelium to lymphocytes and mononuclear phagocytes housed in a basolateral pocket.

icons.label: Organoid
icons.description: Budded epithelial organoid section with a continuous single-cell layer, central lumen, and crypt-like outward buds.
icons.biologicalBasis: Intestinal organoids organize as polarized epithelium surrounding a lumen; crypt domains bud outward as growth and lumen mechanics remodel the wall.

icons.label: Organoid in Matrigel
icons.description: Several budded organoids embedded at different depths inside a transparent extracellular-matrix dome.
icons.biologicalBasis: Matrigel or related matrices provide a 3D basement-membrane-like environment that supports organoid polarization and budding.

icons.label: Organoids on plate
icons.description: Top view of a culture well containing multiple organoids with variable lumen and budding morphology.
icons.biologicalBasis: Organoid cultures are morphologically heterogeneous, containing cystic, bulged, and crypt-budded structures within the same well.

icons.label: Muscle cell
icons.description: Long multinucleated skeletal muscle fiber with peripheral nuclei, repeated sarcomeric striations, and bundled myofibrils.
icons.biologicalBasis: Skeletal myofibers are syncytia; aligned sarcomeres create cross-striations while nuclei reside beneath the peripheral sarcolemma.

icons.label: Nerve cell
icons.description: Neuron with soma, nucleus and nucleolus, branching dendrites, axon hillock, myelinated axon segments, and terminal arbor.
icons.biologicalBasis: Neurons receive input through dendrites and conduct action potentials along axons; myelin is interrupted at nodes of Ranvier.

icons.label: Cardiac cell
icons.description: Branched cardiomyocyte with central nucleus, sarcomeric striations, mitochondria, and dark intercalated discs.
icons.biologicalBasis: Cardiomyocytes are branched striated cells joined end-to-end by intercalated discs containing mechanical and electrical junctions.

icons.label: Liver cells
icons.description: Hepatocyte plate with polygonal cells, central nuclei, binucleation, bile canaliculi, and adjacent sinusoid.
icons.biologicalBasis: Hepatocytes form one- to two-cell-thick plates; apical borders create bile canaliculi while basal surfaces face fenestrated sinusoids.

icons.label: Fibroblast
icons.description: Spread spindle fibroblast with tapering processes, elongated nucleus, actin fibers, rough ER, and secreted collagen fibers.
icons.biologicalBasis: Activated fibroblasts spread on extracellular matrix and synthesize collagen-rich matrix using expanded rough ER and Golgi.

icons.label: Stromal cell
icons.description: Irregular stellate stromal support cell with oval nucleus, long matrix-contacting processes, and extracellular fibers.
icons.biologicalBasis: Mesenchymal stromal cells extend processes through extracellular matrix and provide structural and paracrine niche support.

icons.label: Adipocyte
icons.description: Unilocular adipocyte with one dominant lipid droplet, extremely thin cytoplasmic rim, and peripheral flattened nucleus.
icons.biologicalBasis: White adipocytes store neutral lipid in one large droplet that displaces the nucleus and organelles to the cell periphery.

icons.label: Cell
icons.description: General eukaryotic cell with plasma membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, nucleolus, mitochondria, ER, and Golgi.
icons.biologicalBasis: A eukaryotic cell is compartmentalized by membrane-bound organelles that separate genome maintenance, biosynthesis, trafficking, and energy production.

icons.label: Nucleus
icons.description: Nucleus with double envelope, nuclear pores, peripheral chromatin, euchromatin, and a dense nucleolus.
icons.biologicalBasis: The nuclear envelope is continuous with ER and perforated by pore complexes; nucleoli assemble ribosomal subunits within chromatin-containing nucleoplasm.

icons.label: Mitochondrion
icons.description: Cutaway mitochondrion with outer membrane, inner boundary membrane, folded cristae, matrix, and mitochondrial DNA.
icons.biologicalBasis: Oxidative-phosphorylation complexes occupy the cristae-rich inner membrane, while the matrix contains metabolic enzymes, ribosomes, and mitochondrial DNA.

icons.label: ER
icons.description: Interconnected rough ER cisternae continuous with the nuclear envelope and studded by cytosolic ribosomes.
icons.biologicalBasis: Rough ER ribosomes synthesize secreted and membrane proteins into flattened cisternae for folding and quality control.

icons.label: Golgi
icons.description: Polarized Golgi stack with cis and trans faces, flattened cisternae, and incoming and budding transport vesicles.
icons.biologicalBasis: Golgi cisternae modify and sort biosynthetic cargo as it moves from the cis entry face toward the trans-Golgi network.

icons.label: Vesicle
icons.description: Membrane-bound transport vesicle with lipid bilayer, luminal cargo, and a partial protein coat.
icons.biologicalBasis: Transport vesicles bud with selective coats and cargo adaptors, then fuse with target membranes using tethering and SNARE machinery.

icons.label: DNA
icons.description: Antiparallel double helix with sugar-phosphate backbones, paired bases, major groove, and minor groove.
icons.biologicalBasis: DNA stores information in complementary base pairing while the helical geometry creates major and minor grooves recognized by proteins.

icons.label: RNA
icons.description: Single-stranded RNA with ribose-phosphate backbone, exposed bases, stem-loop hairpin, and 5-prime/3-prime direction.
icons.biologicalBasis: RNA is usually single-stranded but forms intramolecular base-paired stems and loops that support recognition and catalysis.

icons.label: Protein
icons.description: Folded protein ribbon showing alpha helices, beta sheet, connecting loops, and a small ligand-binding pocket.
icons.biologicalBasis: Protein tertiary structure packs secondary-structure elements into a three-dimensional fold whose surface pockets support molecular recognition.

icons.label: Antibody
icons.description: Y-shaped IgG with paired heavy chains, paired light chains, hinge, Fc stem, and two antigen-binding tips.
icons.biologicalBasis: Immunoglobulin heavy and light variable domains form two antigen-binding sites, while the Fc region recruits immune effector mechanisms.

icons.label: Virus
icons.description: Enveloped icosahedral virus with genome-containing capsid, lipid envelope, and surface attachment spikes.
icons.biologicalBasis: Many animal viruses enclose a nucleocapsid within a host-derived lipid envelope bearing glycoprotein spikes used for receptor binding and entry.

icons.label: Bacterium
icons.description: Rod-shaped bacillus with layered envelope, cytoplasm, nucleoid, ribosomes, pili, and flagellum.
icons.biologicalBasis: Bacteria lack a membrane-bound nucleus; chromosomal DNA occupies a nucleoid, ribosomes fill the cytoplasm, and surface appendages mediate adhesion or motility.

icons.label: UMAP
icons.description: UMAP scatter plot with several irregularly shaped colored clusters, local density variation, and a small legend.
icons.biologicalBasis: UMAP projects high-dimensional neighborhood relationships into a low-dimensional embedding; separated point clouds conventionally denote cell states or clusters.

icons.label: Volcano
icons.description: Volcano plot with fold-change and significance axes, dashed thresholds, dense neutral center, and highlighted wings.
icons.biologicalBasis: Volcano plots combine effect size with statistical significance so strongly changed, well-supported features appear in the upper outer regions.

icons.label: Heatmap
icons.description: Expression heatmap with labeled red-blue matrix, row and column dendrograms, and a continuous color scale.
icons.biologicalBasis: Heatmaps encode values by color while hierarchical dendrograms expose similarity-based ordering of rows and columns.

icons.label: Bar plot
icons.description: Bar chart with labeled categories, baseline, ticks, varied heights, error bars, and legend swatches.
icons.biologicalBasis: Bar height encodes a category-level statistic; error bars conventionally show uncertainty or dispersion and require a defined summary measure.

icons.label: Box plot
icons.description: Grouped box-and-whisker plot with medians, interquartile boxes, whiskers, and outliers.
icons.biologicalBasis: A box plot displays median and interquartile range, with whisker and outlier rules summarizing distribution tails.

icons.label: Violin
icons.description: Grouped violin plot with mirrored densities, inner quartile boxes, medians, and sparse observations.
icons.biologicalBasis: Violin width represents estimated probability density while internal summaries anchor median and interquartile range.

icons.label: Scatter
icons.description: XY scatter plot with varied observations, regression line, confidence band, ticks, and axis labels.
icons.biologicalBasis: Scatter plots show paired measurements; a fitted trend and uncertainty band summarize association without replacing the raw observations.

icons.label: Line plot
icons.description: Two-series line plot with markers, axes, ticks, legend, and uncertainty ribbons.
icons.biologicalBasis: Line charts connect ordered observations such as time points; distinct markers and uncertainty bands clarify series and variability.

icons.label: Donut
icons.description: Donut chart with separated colored sectors, proportional arc lengths, labels, and legend.
icons.biologicalBasis: Sector angle encodes part-to-whole proportion, while a central opening preserves the ring structure used by a donut chart.

icons.label: Flow cytometry
icons.description: Flow-cytometry dot-density plot with logarithmic-looking axes, quadrant gates, clusters, and percentages.
icons.biologicalBasis: Flow plots display single-event fluorescence measurements; gates partition phenotypic populations and are interpreted with controls.

icons.label: Survival
icons.description: Kaplan–Meier plot with two stepped survival curves, censor ticks, axes, legend, and risk-table hint.
icons.biologicalBasis: Kaplan–Meier estimates change only at events; censor marks identify observations whose subsequent survival time is unknown.

icons.label: Network
icons.description: Biological interaction network with typed nodes, directed and inhibitory edges, modules, and legend.
icons.biologicalBasis: Network diagrams encode entities as nodes and relationships as edges; arrowheads or T-bars distinguish activation from inhibition.

icons.label: Dendrogram
icons.description: Hierarchical clustering dendrogram with unequal branch lengths, leaves, labels, and a cut threshold.
icons.biologicalBasis: A dendrogram records agglomerative merge order and height; a horizontal cut defines clusters at a chosen dissimilarity.

icons.label: Western blot
icons.description: Western blot membrane with sample lanes, molecular-weight ladder, realistic bands, lane labels, and loading control.
icons.biologicalBasis: Immunoblot band position estimates molecular mass and band intensity reflects target abundance only after appropriate loading normalization.

icons.label: Sequencer
icons.description: Benchtop DNA sequencer with sample bay, touchscreen run trace, status lights, vents, and reagent compartment.
icons.biologicalBasis: Benchtop sequencers combine fluidics, optical or electrical detection, temperature control, and run-control electronics.

icons.label: Microscope
icons.description: Compound light microscope with binocular head, rotating objectives, stage, condenser, focus knobs, illuminator, and base.
icons.biologicalBasis: Compound microscopes form magnified images using objective and eyepiece systems while the stage, condenser, and focus drive position the specimen and illumination.

icons.label: Flask
icons.description: Erlenmeyer flask with narrow neck, graduations, glass wall, liquid meniscus, and suspended culture material.
icons.biologicalBasis: The conical vessel supports mixing with reduced splashing; a curved meniscus and graduations communicate liquid volume.

icons.label: Test tube
icons.description: Glass test tube containing liquid, curved bottom, meniscus, wall thickness, and rack supports.
icons.biologicalBasis: A test tube is a cylindrical vessel with a rounded closed end; the liquid surface forms a meniscus against the wall.

icons.label: Petri dish
icons.description: Top-view petri dish with lid rim, agar surface, colonies of different sizes, and a streak path.
icons.biologicalBasis: Microbial colonies expand clonally on a nutrient-gel surface and differ in size, opacity, margin, and pigmentation.

icons.label: Cell dish
icons.description: Top-view cell-culture dish with lid rim, pink medium, adherent cell islands, and a liquid meniscus.
icons.biologicalBasis: Adherent cultured cells spread across the treated plastic surface beneath a shallow layer of buffered culture medium.

icons.label: 96-well plate
icons.description: Perspective 96-well plate with 8×12 wells, rim, row/column cues, and differently filled assay wells.
icons.biologicalBasis: A standard 96-well plate arranges wells in eight rows and twelve columns for parallel liquid handling and optical assays.

icons.label: Pipette
icons.description: Single-channel micropipette with plunger, volume display, tip ejector, finger hook, shaft, and disposable tip.
icons.biologicalBasis: Air-displacement micropipettes use a piston to aspirate and dispense an adjustable microliter volume through a disposable tip.

icons.label: PCR tubes
icons.description: Eight-tube PCR strip with hinged caps, tapered reaction chambers, sample volumes, and connected top rail.
icons.biologicalBasis: Thin-walled PCR tubes promote rapid thermal transfer and are commonly supplied in connected strips with evaporation-limiting caps.

icons.label: Centrifuge
icons.description: Benchtop microcentrifuge with open lid, rotor, tube positions, hinge, control panel, and safety latch.
icons.biologicalBasis: A centrifuge rotor subjects samples to radial acceleration; balanced tube placement and a locking lid are essential operating features.

icons.label: Syringe
icons.description: Medical syringe with barrel, graduations, plunger, gasket, hub, needle, bevel, and contained fluid.
icons.biologicalBasis: Plunger displacement changes barrel volume, moving fluid through the hub and hollow beveled needle.

icons.label: Vial
icons.description: Capped laboratory vial with transparent wall, septum, label, liquid meniscus, and bottom curvature.
icons.biologicalBasis: Laboratory vials combine a chemically resistant container with a sealed cap or septum for storage and sampling.

icons.label: Incubator
icons.description: CO2 incubator with insulated cabinet, windowed inner door, shelves, sensor panel, water tray, and culture vessels.
icons.biologicalBasis: Cell-culture incubators regulate temperature, CO2, and humidity to stabilize medium pH and prevent evaporation.

icons.label: -80 freezer
icons.description: Upright ultra-low freezer with insulated outer door, inner compartments, latch, gasket, and −80 °C display.
icons.biologicalBasis: Ultra-low freezers use thick insulation, sealed compartments, and staged refrigeration to maintain approximately −80 °C storage.

icons.label: Balance
icons.description: Analytical balance with draft shield, weighing pan, leveling feet, display, and control keys.
icons.biologicalBasis: Analytical balances isolate the weighing pan from air currents and vibration to measure small mass changes reproducibly.

icons.label: Workstation
icons.description: Scientific workstation with monitor, plotted analysis, keyboard, mouse, tower, and data indicators.
icons.biologicalBasis: A workstation icon is grounded by recognizable input devices and a display showing scientific analysis rather than a generic screen glyph.

icons.label: Database
icons.description: Stacked cylindrical database with multiple disk layers, indexed records, input/output arrows, and status indicators.
icons.biologicalBasis: The stacked-cylinder convention represents persistent structured storage; layers and arrows communicate records and data transfer.

icons.label: Mouse model
icons.description: Laboratory mouse in side profile with detailed ear, eye, whiskers, paws, tail, and body contour.
icons.biologicalBasis: The laboratory mouse has a compact rodent body plan with prominent pinnae, vibrissae, digit-bearing paws, and a long tapering tail.

icons.label: Target
icons.description: Folded protein surface with a concave binding pocket, contacting small molecule, and interaction markers.
icons.biologicalBasis: Ligand binding depends on three-dimensional shape and complementary noncovalent contacts within a protein pocket.

icons.label: Drug
icons.description: Two-piece capsule with translucent shell halves, seam, internal granules, and subtle printed dose mark.
icons.biologicalBasis: Hard capsules consist of telescoping cap and body components that enclose powder, pellets, or granules for oral delivery.
